newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO'S NAFIN SAYS TO ISSUE 1 BLN PESOS IN BONDS.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO'S NAFIN SAYS TO ISSUE 1 BLN PESOS IN BONDS.

text.p: Mexican development bank Nacional Financiera (Nafin) said it would issue one billion pesos in bank development bonds in a public offering on Thursday.
The three-year coupon bonds will have an interest rate tied to the TIIE interbank rate and be subject to a rate revision every 28 days, Nafin said in a news release on Wednesday.
"To this end, Nafin yesterday held an auction among financial institutions with the objective of raising money for lending to companies," the statement said.
"The rate at which the instruments were issued was an excellent level for this type of paper, given that it was TIIE minus 0.5494 percent."
The 28-day TIIE rate was 20.38 percent on Wednesday.
Demand was 4.5 times the amount offered for the instruments, which have been dubbed NAFTIIEs, Nafin said.
The lead managers were Banco Bilbao Vizcaya, Banamex, Banco Internacional, Invex Casa de Bolsa, Valores Mexicanos Casa de Bolsa, Ixe Casa de Bolsa and Casa de Bolsa Inverlat, Nafin said.
The bonds, which have a nominal value of 10,000 pesos, were placed at a weighted average price of 10,124 pesos, Nafin said.
On July 17, Nafin issued 1.5 billion pesos worth of bank development bonds at 18- and 36-month terms. Nafin said that was its first issue of the year.
